stem: Plant X is still a major iron and steel plant in China because __________. (1) there is agglomeration of heavy industries (2) its production facilities have been upgraded (3) there is abundant cheap labour supply
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: candidates choosing Option B might have mistaken iron and steel industry in China as being labour intensive. Iron and steel production is capital- and technology-intensive, so the reasons are the agglomeration of heavy industries and upgraded production facilities.

stem: Which of the following are the possible consequences of inappropriate use of chemical fertilizer in Southern California? (1) underground water pollution (2) eutrophication (3) salinization of soil
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: candidates choosing this option might be unaware of the rising contaminated underground water towards the surface during the hot dry summer in Southern California. Fertilizer chemicals leach into groundwater, cause eutrophication through nutrient runoff, and build up salts in the soil.

stem: What are the major causes of the high rate of deforestation in the rainforest in the Brazilian Amazon? (1) high population growth (2) poverty (3) rapid urbanisation
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: candidates choosing this option might have mistaken urban development, which cleared a much smaller area of Amazon forest when compared with economic development, as a 'major' cause.

stem: Refer to the figure below, which shows a section of coast.
Which of the following manufacturing activities is raw material-oriented?
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: candidates might have thought that car manufacturing is a manufacturing procedure which involves many large and heavy raw materials. Cheese making is strongly tied to its perishable raw material (milk), so it must locate near milk production.

stem: Refer to the photograph below, which shows land use X in Hong Kong.

Which of the following are possible consequences caused by the rise of the global mean sea level? (1) an increase in wave erosion (2) the resettlement of the people who live in coastal lowlands (3) higher frequency of tropical cyclones
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: candidates might have thought that the formation of tropical cyclones results from the rise of the global mean sea level. A higher sea level allows waves to reach further inland and erodes coastal land, and coastal lowlands become more flood-prone, prompting resettlement.

stem: Which of the following is/are the location advantage(s) of the Kai Tak Cruise Terminal (1269 and 1369)? (1) proximity to Kwun Tong Typhoon Shelter (2) accessible by railway (3) deep waterfront
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: candidates might have shown a misunderstanding of the nature and function of a cruise terminal. Large cruise ships require deep water frontage to berth, so the deep waterfront is the location advantage; a typhoon shelter and railway access are not advantages for a cruise terminal.

stem: Which of the following is the ecological impact brought about by climate change?
options: southward migration of biomes in the Southern Hemisphere
intensified coral bleaching in the polar region
more frequent extreme rainfall in Hong Kong
fewer forest fires in the Amazon rainforest
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: extreme rainfall is primarily a meteorological event, not an ecological impact. As the Earth warms, the climatic zones that support particular biomes shift polewards, so biomes migrate southward in the Southern Hemisphere. Coral bleaching is strongest in warm tropical waters, not the polar regions.

stem: How does tree planting mitigate the urban heat island effect? (1) increases evapotranspiration (2) absorbs more carbon dioxide (3) provides more tree shading
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: candidates might have confused urban heat island effect with global warming. Trees cool the local urban environment through evapotranspiration and by shading surfaces from solar radiation. Absorbing carbon dioxide mitigates global warming, not the local urban heat island.

stem: Which of the following are the possible problems brought about by urban encroachment in Hong Kong? (1) a loss of farmland (2) a disruption of rural lifestyle (3) a higher risk of flooding
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: candidates were unable to recognise the impact of replacing rural vegetation and farmland with built-up areas, roads and other impermeable surfaces. Such surfaces prevent infiltration and raise runoff, increasing flood risk, while the loss of farmland disrupts rural lifestyles.

stem: Which of the following is/are the example(s) of human input in organic farming? (1) sunlight (2) crop residues (3) genetically modified seeds
explanation: HKEAA briefing note: organic farming emphasises natural processes. Sunlight is a natural input, not a human one. Crop residues used as compost or mulch are a human input, whereas genetically modified seeds are excluded from organic farming.
